newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia submits draft on concessions to parliament.
newsitem.headline: Serbia submits draft on concessions to parliament.

text.p: Serbia's government has submitted to parliament a draft law giving up to 30-year concessions to domestic and foreign companies for using natural resources, Belgrade daily Politika said on Wednesday.
Rights can be granted for a maximum of 30 years under equal terms for foreign and domestic firms.

The government will grant concessions for exploration and exploitation of mineral ores, operation, renewal and development of forests, construction of hunting facilities and game breeding and hunting, Politika daily said.
Interested parties can also compete for construction, maintenance and operation of water management facilities -- dams and accumulation lakes -- and water supply and irrigation systems.

Foreign and domestic companies can build, maintain and use energy facilities, gas and oil pipelines, roads, railways, airports, utilities systems, telecommunications, develop river and lake banks, build spas and participate in other activities of general interest.
Companies will compete for the concession through a public tender, pay for its use and hand over facilities to the owner (the Republic of Serbia) after the agreed date expires.
Serbia also plans to set up an agency to grant and supervise concessions running, Politika said.
The agency will call public tenders, select the most successful bidders and propose them to the government.
Concessioners will enjoy rights under the local laws. Participation of foreign companies will be in line with international investment protection agreements signed by Yugoslavia and Serbia.

Proceeds from the concessions will go to Serbia's state coffers except for public utilities when receipts go to muncipal authorities, Politika said. -- Beti Bilandzic, Belgrade newsroom, + 381 11 222 4305
